packageRules.description: One PR per repo per week for every minor and patch update (group:allNonMajor supplies the groupName). Automerges on green checks. Majors stay separate, unautomerged, and behind dashboard approval. Pins, digests and github-actions have their own rules below.

A pin or a digest re-pin changes no code: it locks an already-resolved version to an exact reference. Without this rule such a PR clears the 3-day age gate and then sits open forever, because the automerge rules above reach only the github-actions manager and npm patch / devDependency minor updates. img-zen#33 (a docker digest) and lumira#98 (pin dependencies) each stalled that way. The identity, payment and lint-schema rule below still wins, because later rules override earlier ones. automerge alone was not enough: the top-level minimumReleaseAge still applied, so renovate/stability-days stayed pending forever and platformAutomerge could never fire. lumira#98 sat that way with every other check green. An age gate is meaningless for a pin, which resolves to a version that already shipped.

Identity, payment and lint-schema packages never auto-merge, and never ride inside a group. The rules above auto-merge every patch (dependencies included) and every devDependency minor, which is the right default for the long tail but wrong for these three. groupName is nulled deliberately: better-auth 1.6.30 -> 1.7.1 auto-merged on green because it was folded into a grouped patch-and-minor PR, so the bump was never looked at on its own - automerge:false alone is ambiguous for a package sitting inside an auto-merging group, and ungrouping is what actually makes this rule bite. 1.7 queries the account model on a new issuer column that did not exist, so every Microsoft sign-in callback returned 500 for two days; nothing in CI exercises a real OAuth callback and sessions last seven days, so it stayed hidden. @biomejs/biome is schema-version-coupled - a bump needs a paired 'biome migrate' that an auto-merge cannot run, and a biome minor once broke the Lint gate on main for exactly that reason. stripe follows the same principle: identity and money bumps wait for a human who reads the changelog.

Renovate never edits package-manager override entries (pnpm.overrides, overrides, pnpm-workspace overrides). Those are per-major security floors maintained by hand (transitive-cve-override). Renovate reads a key like brace-expansion@1 as a dependency and proposed cross-major security bumps such as brace-expansion@1 to v5, which removes the default export minimatch 3 needs (crc-ready5-app#207: expand is not a function). allowedVersions cannot fix this for vulnerability PRs, because Renovate appends its generated vulnerability rule (allowedVersions set to the fixed version) after every user packageRule, so the user allowedVersions is overridden. enabled:false survives, because the generated rule sets no enabled flag unless vulnerabilityAlerts.enabled is configured, and it is not here.
